recompute.summary:
The new plans and the published figures are reproduced: with growth.py's conventions my independent plain-Python engine matches the 30 dumped paths and then all 2,000 paths to the cent (7,548,000 balances, max difference 0.000000 EUR; money paid in, stop weeks and times at zero identical). A fresh growth.resampled run summarises to exactly growth.json['resampled'] for all 27 plans.

One correction is needed before the pictures: **the "fall of the balance as seen" is understated for the fast-start plans**. growth.path_measures takes its first high at the end of week one, so a fall from the opening 1,000 EUR is not counted. For F and FS at half edge the median goes from 32.2 % to 36.8 % and the 9-in-10 figure from 50.0 % to 52.6 %; C2, P, the R plans and Da move by 1 to 4 points. A, A05, A025, D1 and A05S do not move. The fall from the high with payments set aside (the criterion measure), the gains and the other seven measures are identical to mine on all 204,000 paths.

- **My text reading vs growth.py:** the loss budget, ratchet, cap, soft steps, Da / D1 multiplier and F bands had no difference once the known week-unit convention was aligned. Only the stop of FS and A05S differed, in two ways the text leaves open:
  - **When it is read:** growth.py reads the stop at closed trades only, so it fires at the first close after the 12th payment, not at the payment itself.
  - **Open positions:** after the stop it books closes until the next signal, then drops the rest.
  - **Effect:** on all 2,000 paths medians move by at most about 120 EUR and the share stopped by 0.1 point. Immaterial.
- **Edge cases on growth.py's own engine:** 54 of 54 synthetic checks pass (bracket budgets, ratchet, no trade at zero left, 250 EUR soft steps, multipliers, F bands, FS arming and level, A05S from the start). Four of my own test expectations were wrong on the first pass and were corrected.
- **Criterion:** only A025 stays at or under 25 % in both cases (10.5 % and 23.6 %), as the file says. Read after every closed trade instead of at week ends it is 12.0 % and 24.8 %, so it passes by 0.2 point.
- **To say with the pictures:**
  - "Weeks under the high" is a lower bound: the longest stretch is still running at the end in 15 to 22 % of paths at half edge for the flat stakes and F. For stopped plans it measures the freeze, not a recovery.
  - FS has the same fall figures as F (59.1 % / 68.1 %), because the deep falls come before the stop is armed.
  - A stopped FS account with worthless rules has lost about 3,700 EUR typically and 9,100 at worst.

In the first year it costs about 1,700 EUR. The longest run of losing trades in three years is typically 18 trades (about 11 stakes): about 5 % of the account at 0.5 %, about 45 % if it falls in the two months at 5 %.'

The plan shown is not that one: its falls of the first months go to 42 % typically and 59 % one time in ten; after the first year it holds 16 % typically and 24 % one time in ten when the robot is at half of paper, but 27 % and 40 % when the rules are worthless.'

findings.what: FS over A05S, A05, D1 and P is defensible only if the user is told that 'no 50 % loss' holds in euros and after the first year, not in % during the first three months. A05S should be shown next to FS as the calm alternative; I would not replace FS.
findings.evidence: At half edge, FS against A05S: gain at 12 months +3,358 against +1,245 (on paper +6,474 against +2,489), at 36 months +17,228 against +14,617; deepest fall 42.5 % typical / 59.1 % one in ten against 15.1 % / 21.0 %; a fall of 50 % or more in 23.7 % of paths against 0 %; first-year fall in euros 1,922 / 3,218 against 933 / 1,601; more than a year under the high 27.2 % against 17.9 %; false stops 8.5 % against 4.2 %. P at half edge: deepest fall 57.7 % typical / 87.0 % one in ten, +3,357 at 12 months, 1 in 10 -2,556 at 36 months, in one path in ten the robot receives 5,000 EUR or less.
findings.fix: Show two plans side by side. FS: 'fast first months, calm after; the account can halve in the first three months, on 2,000 to 3,000 EUR'. A05S (0.5 % always, stop at -25 % from the start): 'never fast: about +1,200 after a year at half of paper against +3,400, but no fall beyond about 21 % nine times out of ten and never a halving; if the rules are worthless it takes 20 months and 4,500 EUR to find out instead of 11 months and 3,700'. If the user means 'never -50 %, even on 2,000 EUR', A05S is his plan; if he means euros and the long run, FS.

findings.what: The hands 1.11 cannot run FS as simulated without changes or several manual edits on exact dates; the simulated first two months imply a daily loss allowance of 30 %.
findings.evidence: Read in live_ai/mql5/ClaudeMains.mq5 (version 1.11): InpMaxRiskPct is one fixed input (default 1.0; cap = balance x InpMaxRiskPct); InpDailyLossPct = 6 % of the day's starting balance; InpKillPct = 50 on CM_start, the reference that follows deposits (max(reference + deposit, equity right after)), tested on equity at every pass; Capital() keeps the reference following deposits even when InpKillPct = 0; InpResetLocks deletes CM_start and restarts the reference from the current balance. Simulation: no daily lock at all; stop read on the balance at closes; schedule read on max(balance, money paid in). The hands keep no separate count of money paid in (CM_start is also raised to the equity).
findings.fix: Needed: (1) risk cap as a schedule 5 / 2 / 1 / 0.5 % read on max(balance, net deposits), with a net-deposit counter separate from CM_start, and the brain sizing with the same schedule; by hand it is three edits of InpMaxRiskPct (at 3,000, 6,000 and 12,000 EUR), and a forgotten edit means 5 % on 12,000 EUR. (2) Daily lock in stakes: 6 stakes = 30 % of the balance in months 1-2, 12 % in months 3-5, 6 % in months 6-11, 3 % after; left at 6 % it blocks the day after one or two losing trades at 5 %, which the simulation does not do. (3) Stop: InpKillPct = 25 with a new 'armed once net deposits reach 12,000' input; by hand InpKillPct must stay 0 for eleven months and be set to 25 right after the twelfth payment, never through InpResetLocks (that restarts the reference at the current balance: a softer stop than simulated). Expect it to fire at once in about 3 % of half-edge paths and 60 % of worthless ones. (4) Say that the real stop reads equity continuously, so it fires somewhat earlier and more often than the simulated 8.5 %; that 'nothing more is paid in' after the stop is the user's discipline; Friday close, slippage and the broker's real leverage are not in the curves.

critique.summary:
The sentences about plan FS are true to the cells of growth.json, with one exception, but they cannot be said as they are: the euro figures for the early falls are too low, and several things the user asked about by name are left out. No conclusion flips.

**1. Truth of each sentence**
- The gain sentences match the cells: +6,474 and +44,871 on paper, +3,358 and +17,228 at half of paper, -3,663 with worthless rules (stopped in 95.4 % of paths, median month 11, 12,000 EUR paid in).
- The falls after the first year match: 15.5 % typical and 23.6 % one time in ten, against 29.8 / 40.9 for a flat 1 % and 35.2 / 54.8 for the unprotected fast start. They should be rounded to 16 % and 24 %.
- The 12 weeks (25 one time in ten) for the balance as seen match.
- **Wrong figure:** "900 to 1,300 EUR, 1,800 to 2,700 one time in ten". On all 2,000 paths at week ends, the deepest fall of the first 12 months for FS is:

| Scenario | Median | 1 in 10 | Worst |
|---|---|---|---|
| On paper | 1,438 | 2,242 | 4,523 |
| Half of paper | 1,922 | 3,218 | 5,787 |
| Worthless rules | 3,767 | 5,263 | 8,527 |

- "Can lose half" understates how often: a fall of 50 % or more happens in 12 % of paths on paper and 24 % at half of paper. It comes in the first three months in more than 80 % of cases, on about 2,000 EUR paid in.

**2. What is left out**
- **False stops:** on the 8.5 % of paths stopped at half of paper, the user is typically 2,000 EUR down (4,400 one time in ten). The same paths without the stop end at +6,100, and 81 % of them end in gain.
- **The stop is not "25 %":** with worthless rules, 63 % of the stops fire on the day the stop is armed. The typical loss is 3,700 EUR on 12,000 paid in (31 %); one time in ten it is 5,500, at worst 9,100.
- **Arming point:** 12,000 EUR is a sound choice. At 6,000 the false stops rise to 34 %; at 18,000 the worthless case costs about 1,200 EUR more.
- **A good year, then worthless:** the stop takes about ten months to fire. A paper year's gain of +6,474 ends at +205; a half-paper year ends at -2,139 (-5,138 one time in ten). FS is still the best of the plans tested in that case; only 0.25 % always is about level with it.
- **"Wait a year":** at half of paper, the robot's own gain stays more than a year under its high in 27 % of FS paths (18 months one time in ten).
- **"Fast":** FS is ahead of a flat 1 % only for six to nine months (2,982 against 1,276 EUR at month 6 on paper). After a year the two are level (6,474 against 6,274). In euros the gain per month keeps rising; what calms down is the risk in %.
- **First two months:** the worst week typically costs 30 to 33 % of the account, about half one time in ten.

**3. Consecutive losses**
The lead's reading is confirmed: no declared plan makes losing runs rarer or shorter, only cheaper.
- Longest run of losing weeks for FS: 4 typical, 5 one time in ten, 7 worst at half of paper; 4 / 4 / 8 on paper.
- Longest run of losing months: 3 / 5 / 11 at half of paper; 2 / 3 / 7 on paper.
- A run of four or more losing weeks happens in 57 % of three-year paths at half of paper and 53 % on paper.
- After the first year such a run costs about 12 % of the account at 0.5 % (4,000 to 4,800 EUR), against 21 to 24 % at a flat 1 % (8,300 to 12,000 EUR).
- The longest run of losing trades is typically 18 (about 11 stakes). This is my own approximate count on all signals, not a figure of the study.

**4. Is FS defensible?**
- FS does not meet the declared criterion under any reading (59 % and 68 % one time in ten; counting only after month 12, 24 % and 40 %).
- A05S misses it by a hair (21.0 % and 26.5 %). Only A025 qualifies.
- FS is defensible as the plan closest to "very fast at the start, calm afterwards", and it finds worthless rules sooner and cheaper than A05S (month 11 and -3,700 against month 20 and -4,500).
- I would not replace it. I would show A05S beside it and say plainly that "no 50 % loss" holds for FS in euros and after the first year, not in % during the first three months.

**5. Realism**
- The 5 % start is what lets the ten rules trade at FP's minimum lots: at 1 % of 1,000 EUR, 54 % of signals cannot be placed; at 5 %, 1.3 %.
- The hands 1.11 have one fixed risk cap, a 6 % daily lock and a stop that is not gated by money paid in. FS needs either a risk schedule, a daily lock in stakes and an "armed at 12,000 paid in" input, or five manual edits on exact dates.
- The simulated first two months imply a daily loss allowance of 30 %.
